children: Delinquencies increased in several retail loan categories in the September quarter, with gold, consumer durable, personal and two-wheeler loans showing signs of stress even as retail credit portfolio expanded 18.8 percent YoY to Rs 185.2 trillion, a report by CRIF has said.

The share of loans overdue by 31-180 days in the consumer durable segment rose to 1.8 percent from 1.6 percent in the June quarter, while gold loan delinquencies increased to 1.6 percent from 1.3 percent.
Personal loan delinquencies edged up to 2.4 percent from 2.3 percent and two-wheeler to 4.1 percent from 4 percent.

Tractor loan delinquencies rose to 5.3 percent from 4.6 percent. Commercial vehicle loans recorded a sharper increase at 6.1 percent from 5 percent, though it was “largely driven by account closures by a member between July and Sep'26” and may not indicate an organic increase in stress, CRIF said.
Overall, retail loan delinquencies improved, with the portfolio's 31-180 day delinquency ratio declining to 2.6 percent in Q2 from 2.9 percent in June.
Credit card, auto, used car, housing, property, secured and unsecured business, agriculture and education loans also recorded an improvement or remained stable.

“While overall delinquencies improved, certain products-particularly consumer durable loans, tractor loans, and gold loans-registered increases in PAR 31-180 (QoQ), underscoring the need for stronger risk monitoring and a calibrated approach to growth,” CRIF said.
Portfolio growth and lending trends

The total retail credit portfolio stood at Rs 185.2 trillion, up 18.8 percent. Housing loans remained the largest segment at Rs 46.4 trillion, accounting for 25.1 percent of the portfolio, followed by gold loans at Rs 23.3 trillion and secured business loans at Rs 19.6 trillion.

Gold loans grew the fastest among major segments, expanding 60.6 percent YoY, while secured business loans grew 45.2 percent and consumer durable loans 44.5 percent. Property loans grew 22.4 percent and auto loans 18.2 percent.
On a quarterly basis, growth was led by property loans, which rose 7.8 percent, followed by gold loans at 7.5 percent, consumer durables at 6.3 percent and secured business loans at 5.8 percent.
CRIF attributed the expansion to a mix of collateral-backed and consumption-led credit.
PSU banks gain in home loans; NBFCs dominate volumes
Public sector banks increased their share of home loan originations by value to 44.5 percent from 40 percent in the June quarter, supported by lending in loans of more than Rs 75 lakh.
These borrowings accounted for 42.1 percent of home-loan origination value, up from 40.9 percent in the previous quarter.

NBFCs continued to dominate originations by volume in personal loans, accounting for 92.1 percent, and consumer durable loans, at 90.3 percent. In gold loans, NBFCs increased their share of originations by value to 31.4 percent, up around four percentage points from the June quarter.

Gold loan originations by value rose 27.2 percent YoY to Rs 8.15 trillion in Q2 but volumes declined 4.1 percent to 369.4 lakh accounts, reflecting higher average ticket sizes amid elevated gold prices.

CRIF also flagged stress within NBFC portfolios. Personal loan delinquencies in the 91-180 day bucket rose to 1.1 percent from 0.8 percent, driven by NBFCs and loans in the Rs 2 lakh-Rs 10 lakh ticket-size range.
In consumer durable loans, the delinquency rate increased QoQ for NBFCs and loans below Rs 50,000.

Gold loan early-bucket delinquencies, or loans overdue by 31-90 days, rose to 1.3 percent from 0.9 percent in June. Two-wheeler stress was also concentrated in NBFC portfolios, particularly loans below Rs 1 lakh.
The report said consumer durable loans continued to account for the largest share of new-to-credit accounts at 30.7 percent, while gold loans increased their share by around 9 percent.

title: Retail loan stress rises in gold, personal, consumer durable segments: CRIF report
